attrs.label: Psono Image
attrs.description:
Community Edition is free and open source.</br>
Enterprise Edition requires a valid Psono license.

attrs.label: Postgres Image (CAUTION)
attrs.description:
If you are changing this after the postgres directory has been initialized,</br>
STOP! and make sure you have a backup of your data.</br>
Changing this will trigger an one way database upgrade.</br>
You can only select newer versions of postgres.</br>
Selecting an older version will refuse to start.</br>
If something goes wrong, you will have to restore from backup.

attrs.label: Base URL
attrs.description:
The exact URL used to reach Psono from a browser, without a trailing slash.</br>
The web client is a static bundle that is built with this value, so it has to
match how users actually connect.</br>
Examples:</br>
  - http://192.168.1.100:30475</br>
  - https://psono.example.com</br>

attrs.label: Service Name
attrs.description: The name displayed in the web client and in emails.

attrs.label: Server Keys
attrs.description:
Generate all six values at once with:
docker run --rm psono/psono-combo:latest python3 ./psono/generateserverkeys.py

Back them up. They cannot be changed after the first user has registered without losing access to every stored secret.

attrs.label: Secret Key
attrs.description: Random string of 32 characters or more.

attrs.label: Activation Link Secret
attrs.description: Random string of 32 characters or more, used to sign activation links.

attrs.label: Database Secret
attrs.description: Random string of 32 characters or more, used to encrypt data at rest.

attrs.label: Email Secret Salt
attrs.description:
A bcrypt salt, used to hash email addresses so they can be looked up without being stored in clear text.
This is not a random string. It must be a real bcrypt salt, otherwise registration fails with "Invalid salt".
Looks like $2b$12$XUG.sKxC2jmkUvWQjg53.e (29 characters).
On its own: python3 -c 'import bcrypt; print(bcrypt.gensalt().decode())'

schema.valid_chars_error: Please provide a bcrypt salt, for example $2b$12$XUG.sKxC2jmkUvWQjg53.e

attrs.label: Private Key
attrs.description:
Hex encoded NaCl (X25519) private key.
The public key below is derived from this one, so the two have to come from the same generation. Two independently generated keys will not work.

schema.valid_chars_error: Please provide a 64 character lowercase hex string.

attrs.label: Public Key
attrs.description: Hex encoded NaCl (X25519) public key, derived from the private key above.

schema.valid_chars_error: Please provide a 64 character lowercase hex string.

attrs.label: Allowed Domains
attrs.description:
Domains that usernames are allowed to end with.
A user registering as alice@example.com requires example.com to be listed here.

attrs.label: Allowed Hosts
attrs.description:
Host headers the server will answer to.
Leave the default * unless you know you need to restrict it.

attrs.label: Enable Admin Portal API
attrs.description: Required for the Admin Portal (served under /portal) to work.

attrs.label: Number of Reverse Proxies
attrs.description:
Number of reverse proxies in front of Psono, used to parse X-Forwarded-For correctly.
Leave empty when Psono is reached directly.

attrs.label: Authentication Methods
attrs.description:
LDAP, SAML and OIDC require the Enterprise Edition and are configured
from the Admin Portal once enabled here.

attrs.label: Require All Configured Second Factors
attrs.description:
When enabled, users must pass every second factor they configured,
instead of just one of them.

attrs.label: Registration Email Filter
attrs.description:
Restrict registration to these email domains.</br>
Leave empty to accept any email domain.

attrs.label: Allow Custom Server
attrs.description: Let users point the web client at a different Psono server.

attrs.label: Allow Partial User Search By Username
Block Reuse Of Last Passwords
attrs.description:
Number of previous passwords that cannot be reused.</br>
Set to 0 to disable.

attrs.label: YubiKey OTP
attrs.description:
Credentials from https://upgrade.yubico.com/getapikey/.
Only used when YubiKey OTP is an allowed second factor.

attrs.label: Duo
attrs.description: Only used when Duo is an allowed second factor.

attrs.label: Email
attrs.description:
Psono sends account activation, password recovery and share
notification emails.

attrs.label: Enable SMTP
attrs.description:
When disabled, emails are not delivered and accounts have to be
activated manually from the shell.

attrs.label: Cache Type
attrs.description:
Redis speeds up the server and is recommended for more than a
handful of users.

attrs.label: Enable Throttling
attrs.description:
Rate limits login attempts and API calls.</br>
Only disable this for troubleshooting.

attrs.label: Additional Environment Variables
attrs.description: Any Psono setting can be set here by prefixing it with PSONO_, for example PSONO_TIME_SERVER.

attrs.label: Port Bind Mode
attrs.description:
The port bind mode.</br>
- Publish: The port will be published on the host for external access.</br>
- Expose: The port will be exposed for inter-container communication.</br>
- None: The port will not be exposed or published.</br>
Note: If the Dockerfile defines an EXPOSE directive,
the port will still be exposed for inter-container communication regardless of this setting.

1.0.1.readme:
Psono

Psono is a self-hosted, open source password manager for teams.

This app deploys the psono-combo image, which bundles three things behind nginx:

| Path | Component | | --------- | ------------------------------------ | | / | Web client | | /server | REST API (Django + daphne) | | /portal | Admin portal |

Database migrations run automatically on every start.

Before installing

Psono needs six server keys. Generate them all at once:

docker run --rm psono/psono-combo:latest python3 ./psono/generateserverkeys.py

The output is ready to paste field by field:

SECRET_KEY: 'nQ7...64 alphanumeric characters...' ACTIVATION_LINK_SECRET: '...' DB_SECRET: '...' EMAIL_SECRET_SALT: '$2b$12$XUG.sKxC2jmkUvWQjg53.e' PRIVATE_KEY: '302650c3c82f7111c2e8ceb660d32173cdc8c3d7717f1d4f982aad5234648fcb' PUBLIC_KEY: '02da2ad857321d701d754a7e60d0a147cdbc400ff4465e1f57bc2d9fbfeddf0b'

If you would rather not run the image, the same values can be produced separately. The three secrets are plain random strings:

openssl rand -hex 32

EMAIL_SECRET_SALT is a bcrypt salt, not a random string. Psono calls bcrypt.hashpw(email, EMAIL_SECRET_SALT) to store a lookup hash of each email address, so anything that is not a valid salt makes registration fail with Invalid salt:

python3 -c 'import bcrypt; print(bcrypt.gensalt().decode())'

PRIVATE_KEY and PUBLIC_KEY are one X25519 key pair, hex encoded. The public key is derived from the private key, so they must come from the same generation. Two separately generated keys will not work:

python3 -c 'import nacl.encoding from nacl.public import PrivateKey k = PrivateKey.generate() print("PRIVATE_KEY:", k.encode(nacl.encoding.HexEncoder).decode()) print("PUBLIC_KEY: ", k.public_key.encode(nacl.encoding.HexEncoder).decode())'

Copy the six values into the Server Keys section and back them up. They cannot be changed after the first user has registered without losing access to every stored secret.

You also need to set Base URL to the exact URL browsers will use, without a trailing slash (for example http://192.168.1.100:30475 or https://psono.example.com). The web client is a static bundle that is built with this value, so it has to match how users actually connect. If you later move Psono behind a reverse proxy, update Base URL too.

After installing

Register the first account from the Web UI. The username must end with one of the domains listed in Allowed Domains.

Without SMTP configured, no activation email is sent. Activate the account from the TrueNAS shell instead:

docker exec ix-<app-name>-psono-1 \ python3 /root/psono/manage.py verifyuseremail <username>

To reach the admin portal under /portal, promote that account:

docker exec ix-<app-name>-psono-1 \ python3 /root/psono/manage.py promoteuser <username> superuser

Enterprise Edition

Selecting Psono Enterprise Edition switches to psono/psono-combo-enterprise, which requires a valid Psono license. LDAP, SAML and OIDC providers are configured from the admin portal once the matching entry is enabled under Authentication Methods.

Notes

  • The container health check uses /server/info/ rather than /server/healthcheck/. The latter performs an outbound NTP request on every call and is rate limited to 61 requests per hour, so it is unsuitable as a Docker health check.
  • Any setting not exposed in the UI can be set through Additional Environment Variables using the PSONO_ prefix, for example PSONO_TIME_SERVER. See the Psono environment variable reference.
